The section opens immediately below a full-width horizontal rule that closes the preceding 'Summe of the Old Testament' (…where the same are ended.). Two-line display heading in roman capitals: 'OF MOYSES THE AVTHOR OF THE' / 'fiue firſt bookes.' (final E of the first line carries a small stray accent-like mark). Body is ONE continuous justified italic paragraph opened by a ~2-line drop-cap 'M'. LEFT margin carries three roman note-glosses (content summaries); RIGHT margin carries stacked italic Latin source-citations. Catchword 'THE' at foot-right anticipates the next page's 'THE ARGVMENT OF THE BOOKE OF GENESIS.' body.text: OF MOYSES THE AVTHOR OF THE
body.marks: roman display capitals; small stray accent-like mark over final E of THE

body.text: fiue firſt bookes.
MOyſes (ſo called becauſe he was taken from the water, as the name
ſignifieth) was borne in Ægypt. the ſonne of Amram, the ſonne
of Caath, the ſonne of Leui the Patriarch, and ſo of Iacob, Iſaac, and
Abraham. His maruelous deliuerie from drowning, his education, excellent
forme, ſingular wiſdome, heroical vertues, rare dexteritie in al affayres, &
whole life moſt admirable, are gathered out of holie Scriptures, by S. Gre-
gorie Biſhop of Niſſen, into a briefe ſumme, moſt worthie to be read, but
to large for this place. He was borne about the yeare of the world two thou-
ſand foure hundred, long before al prophane writers, yea before manie of
the Painimes falſe goddes, as S. Auguſtin declareth in diuers places of his
moſt excellent booke intituled of the Citie of God. He liued in this world
110. yeares. Of which 40. were in Pharaos court, as the adopted ſonne of
Pharaos daughter: fourtie in baniſhment from Ægypt in Madian: and fourtie
more he gouerned the people of Iſrael. His ſingular prayſes are alſo briefly
touched in the laſt chapter of Deuteromie, added by Ioſue. and in the booke of
Eccleſiaſticus. He di⟨e?⟩d in the deſert, and was buried in the vaile of Moab, ſo
ſecretly that no mortal men knew his ſepulchre, leſt the Iewes, who were very
prone to Idolatrie, should haue adored his bodie with diuine honour, for the
greatnes and multitude of his miracles, and for the ſingular eſtimation, they
had of him for the ſame.
THE

printed 'Deuteromie' (D-e-u-t-e-r-o-m-i-e) — the '-no-' syllable of 'Deuteronomie' is absent on the page. Preserved diplomatically as printed (NOT corrected). Content = Deuteronomy 34 (confirmed by right-margin 'Deut. 34.').

medial vowel glyph is broken/blotted (reads like 'di:d'/'di∴d' at zoom); the d-i-_-d frame plus context ('He di_d in the deſert, and was buried') gives 'died'. Archaic 'dyed' is conceivable but the frame favors 'died'. Flagged per glyph-driven policy.

medial 'ul'/'ti' lightly inked ('m⟨u⟩l⟨ti⟩tude'); word is unambiguous from letter-frame and sense ('greatnes and multitude of his miracles'). Transcribed 'multitude'.
